Qeshm|Iran.f: Qeshm is the largest island in the Persian Gulf and holds Namakdan, one of the world's longest salt caves at over six kilometers.

Duqm|Oman.f: Omani planners see Duqm as a potential alternative to Dubai, especially if shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz were to close.

Espargos|Cabo Verde.f: Espargos grew up around the airport that Italy built in 1939 as a fuel stop on routes from Europe to South America.

Corisco|Eq. Guinea.f: Corisco takes its name from the Portuguese word for lightning, after the gales sailors met around the island.

Djanet|Algeria.f: Djanet is the gateway to Tassili n'Ajjer, whose rock art led Henri Lhote to call it the greatest museum of prehistoric art in the world.

Rabil|Cabo Verde.f: Rabil was founded in the 17th century as Boa Vista's first capital, then lost that status to Sal Rei as sea trade shifted there.

São Pedro|Cabo Verde.f: The airport serving Mindelo on Sao Vicente was renamed in 2012 for the island's famous singer Cesaria Evora.

Sharurah|Saudi Arabia.f: Sharurah is said to be named for the sparks that fly from camel hooves striking the volcanic rocks south of town.

Bordj Badji Mokhtar|Algeria.f: The town was called Bordj Le Prieur in colonial times before being renamed for independence activist Badji Mokhtar (1919-1954).

In Aménas|Algeria.f: The nearby Zarzaitine oil field was found in 1957, began producing in October 1960 and shipped crude by pipeline to La Skhirra.

Rafha|Saudi Arabia.f: Rafha hosted the only refugee camp in the history of the modern Saudi state, opened in 1991 for Iraqis fleeing Saddam Hussein.

Abu Musa|Iran.f: A German company mined red oxide on Abu Musa in the early 1900s, sparking a diplomatic row between Germany and Britain.

Khark|Iran.f: The Dutch East India Company ran Kharg as a free port from 1753 until Mir Muhanna seized its fort in January 1766.

Preguiça|Cabo Verde.f: Preguica became the port of Ribeira Brava after pirate attacks forced Sao Nicolau's older Porto de Lapa to be abandoned in 1653.

Ouani|Comoros.f: In March 2008 Comoran and African Union troops landed on Anjouan and advanced on Ouani to secure its airfield.

Príncipe|São Tomé and Principe.f: Arthur Eddington watched the 1919 solar eclipse from Principe, a key observation that supported Einstein's general relativity.

Praslin|Seychelles.f: Praslin's Vallee de Mai shelters the coco de mer palm, which bears the largest seed in the plant world.

Port Mathurin|Mauritius.f: Francois Leguat and seven Huguenot companions lived over two years in the 1690s on the river bank just east of today's Port Mathurin.
